## Purpose This PR enables prefill dual-batch-overlap (DBO) for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm in data-parallel deployments (attention DP, experts TP via flattened TP, no EP, e.g. `--data-parallel-size 8`). Today `--enable-dbo` splits the prefill batch into two ubatches and runs them as a two-thread ping-pong on a compute stream plus a comm stream, but only the DeepEP-HT prepare/finalize hands its collectives to the comm stream. The naive DP/EP path — which is what a DP deployment without `--enable-expert-parallel` uses — runs its MoE all-gather (dispatch) and reduce-scatter (combine) synchronously on the compute stream, so both streams serialize and DBO buys nothing in prefill. ## Trace Comparison (Conc=64, Prefill) Main (DBO disabled): This PR (DBO enabled, **9.25%** faster per layer): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` and `agentic` workload with server launch commands below: ```bash export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S='10800' export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL='32768' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER='1' export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION='INT4' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE='1' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS='0' export OMP_NUM_THREADS='1' vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --served-model-name 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro' \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend 'mp' \ --kv-cache-dtype 'fp8' \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \ --moe-backend 'aiter' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 2.49}' \ --tokenizer-mode 'deepseek_v4' \ --tool-call-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --reasoning-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --prefill-schedule-interval 8 \ --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --load-format fastsafetensors \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 8192 \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 8192 ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=/shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` ## Test Result ### Benchmark **Fixed sequence length (prefill only):** > Using SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with `OSL=1` to only test prefill duration, so that the received requests across ranks can meet DBO gate in more steps. Concurrency | Version | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | P99 TTFT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | Main (DBO disabled) | 922.68 | — | 922.68 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ 4 | Main (DBO disabled) | 1005.18 | — | 1220.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1016.20 | 1.10% ↑ | 1289.38 | 5.65% ↑ 16 | Main (DBO disabled) | 2140.47 | — | 3912.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 2205.26 | 3.03% ↑ | 3767.09 | 3.72% ↓ 64 | Main (DBO disabled) | 5858.52 | — | 10182.92 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 5477.98 | 6.49% ↓ | 9482.81 | 6.87% ↓ 128 | Main (DBO disabled) | 10858.97 | — | 19695.63 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 10042.61 | 7.52% ↓ | 18934.63 | 3.86% ↓ Overall, the latest results indicate that This PR is primarily beneficial under high-concurrency workloads (`conc=64/128`), where it consistently reduces both average and tail TTFT. However, it introduces small regressions at low concurrency, particularly at `conc=1`. Therefore, the performance benefit appears to scale with concurrency, making the PR more favorable for highly concurrent serving scenarios. **Agentic replay (conc=64):** Version | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Main (DBO disabled) | 703.40 | — | 2,173.93 | — | 44.69 | — This PR (DBO enabled) | 752.46 | 6.97% ↑ | 2,112.09 | 2.85% ↓ | 43.15 | 3.45% ↓ The benchmark results show that enabling DBO in This PR provides an overall performance improvement across all three key metrics. ### Accuracy Test Task | Filter | n-shot | Metric | Main (DBO disabled) | This PR (DBO enabled) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- gsm8k | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ gsm8k | strict-match | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9538 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ ---

nodes.body:
Thanks for this. I reproduced the numbers and tested each part of the change on MI355X (8x, ROCm 10
nightly and the ROCm 7.2.3 nightly, DSV4-Pro, DP8, your launch flags, InferenceX agentic replay at
conc 64).

**Summary**

- The ~30% regression comes from a bug in main's DBO path rather than from the overlap: the eager
  microbatch threads never set their device, so work that uses the current device runs on GPU 0.
  One-line fix below; I'd like to see it go in with this PR.
- With the fix, DBO is at parity with no-DBO end to end (958 vs 917-977 output tok/s over three
  no-DBO runs), and accuracy matches with microbatching actually active (see section 2).
- I could reproduce the failures behind the `positions` slicing and the numpy-int casts. I could not
  reproduce the reasons given for disabling FULL-graph microbatching on ROCm or for the extra profile
  run.
- #46990's changes are gated on `deepep_high_throughput`, so they don't apply on this path.

### 1. Device not set in `_run_ubatches` threads

`_run_ubatches` starts a new thread per microbatch and never sets the device, so the thread's
current device is 0. `_capture_ubatches` already sets it:

```python
        def _ubatch_thread(results, model, ubatch_metadata):
            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(self.device)
            with ubatch_metadata.context:
```

Before the fix:
- With the server idle after startup, GPU 0 was 100% busy and the other seven idle (main: all idle).
- In kernel traces only rank 0's kernels were slow (fused MoE ~1.8x normal). DP ranks wait on each
  other every step, so every rank slows down, which matches the TPOT regression in the description.
- Agentic throughput: 670-717 tok/s with DBO before the fix, 958 after.
- On the ROCm 7.2.3 nightly, DBO without the fix crashed a worker with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`
  (0x1016) in 2 of 6 runs. With the fix, 4 of 4 runs were clean (931-955 tok/s vs 899-938 without
  DBO). Too few runs to call it fixed, and I haven't found the faulting kernel.

### 2. Comm-stream overlap for the naive DP/EP path

Performance: on a prefill-heavy burst (every rank on full 8192-token chunks), the comm stream's RCCL
kernels run on a separate HW queue and the collectives are almost entirely hidden; with them forced
back onto the compute stream the same burst is 20-75% slower (two runs). It is still ~9% slower than
not microbatching at all (3.67 s vs 3.37 s GPU time on rank 0, one clean run). The MoE and several
GEMM kernels run noticeably slower while RCCL overlaps them, so I suspect contention, but I haven't
isolated it.

How often it applies: microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks, so a step is only split if every
rank qualifies. In a gsm8k run with DBO on, most steps that met the threshold weren't split because
some rank opted out; as far as I can tell that was mostly FULL-graph decode (the check in section 3)
and, with prefix caching on, the prefix-cache hazard check. In the agentic replay ~8% of steps were
split at a threshold of 8192, so the end-to-end effect is small either way.

Accuracy: gsm8k (your test plan) and ARC-challenge matched main, but with prefix caching on, DBO
barely split any steps. With prefix caching off, ARC-challenge (25-shot) split ~70 steps and matched
main within error (acc 0.707 vs 0.715, acc_norm 0.730 vs 0.727, ±0.013). That covers prefill
log-likelihoods, not generation.

On the implementation, I'd suggest keeping this in the base class rather than adding a ROCm
subclass: the `_comm_region` handoff is a no-op without DBO, so it could live in
`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular` for all platforms, without the factory swap (which currently
changes the class for every ROCm naive DP/EP user) or the ROCm-only config check. And rather than
having `supports_async()` return `dbo_enabled()` to get past the modular-kernel assert, an explicit
"supports DBO" capability would say what's meant; `supports_async()` is also read by the
shared-experts scheduling on every forward, so overloading it has side effects beyond the assert.

Have you measured DBO with DP+EP on this model? That path already has an overlapping
dispatch/combine, and it would help to know how it compares before adding a second overlap path.
(If you do, note that #46990's ROCm-specific changes on that path, the async-scheduling disable, the
`comm_sms = 0` override and the post-dispatch/combine `synchronize()`, may be unnecessary and likely
cost performance; see the reasoning in ROCm/vllm@1e708140206bce5f0e518b636c7193c18f920bba and
ROCm/vllm@997dce5602326b08431ec28056452e9eb6f7b756. It may be worth trying with them reverted.)

### 3. Disabling microbatching for FULL cudagraphs on ROCm

With this hunk removed, microbatched FULL graphs captured and replayed without errors on both ROCm 10
and ROCm 7.2.3. Microbatched decode was ~1.8x slower per token, so keeping decode out of DBO is
right, but `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` already does that on any platform (with the hunk removed
and a high threshold, decode matched main). I'd drop the platform check. If you have the hipBLASLt
error text and ROCm version, I'd like to look at it.

### 4. Extra profile run on ROCm

With this removed I saw no "Workspace is locked" error, in long-prompt bursts or in a 900 s agentic
run. Do you have a failing config?

### 5. numpy int casts

Reproduced: without them startup fails with `TypeError: failed to specialize argument of type:
numpy.int32` in `build_c128a_topk_metadata`. The numpy value comes from the last split point in
`maybe_create_ubatch_slices`; casting there instead covers every consumer (tested in place of the
casts in this PR):

```python
    all_points = token_split_points + [int(cu_num_tokens[-1])]
```

### 6. Slicing `positions` per microbatch

Reproduced (startup fails with `positions is required for C128A metadata build`). Looks right.

### 7. MTP hidden-buffer offset

From reading the code this looks like a real bug: both microbatch threads write
`_mtp_hidden_buffer` from row 0, and the drafter reads the buffer in token order for the whole step.
It only affects draft quality, not output. The same write is in the other DeepSeek-V4 backends (and
DeepSeek-V4.1 / Qwen4-Exp); should they get the same offset?
@mawong-amd Thanks for your information, I will take a look.

@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize import (
+    naive_dp_ep,
+    naive_dp_ep_rocm,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.naive_dp_ep import (
+    make_moe_prepare_and_finalize_naive_dp_ep,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.naive_dp_ep_rocm import (
+    MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO,
+    _comm_overlap_active,
+)
+
+
+class _RegionProbe(MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.body_ran = False
+
+    def run_comm(self) -> None:
+        with self._comm_region():
+            self.body_ran = True
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def dbo_mocks():
+    return {
+        "yield_switch": MagicMock(),
+        "switch_back": MagicMock(),
+    }
+
+
+def _patch_dbo_calls(dbo_mocks):
+    return (
+        patch.object(
+            naive_dp_ep_rocm,
+            "dbo_yield_and_switch_from_compute_to_comm",
+            dbo_mocks["yield_switch"],
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            naive_dp_ep_rocm,
+            "dbo_switch_to_compute_sync",
+            dbo_mocks["switch_back"],
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def test_comm_region_noop_without_dbo(dbo_mocks):
+    probe = _RegionProbe()
+    patches = _patch_dbo_calls(dbo_mocks)
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=False),
+        patches[0],
+        patches[1],
+    ):
+        probe.run_comm()
+    assert probe.body_ran
+    dbo_mocks["yield_switch"].assert_not_called()
+    dbo_mocks["switch_back"].assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_comm_region_handoff_when_dbo_active(dbo_mocks):
+    probe = _RegionProbe()
+    patches = _patch_dbo_calls(dbo_mocks)
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=True),
+        patch.object(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=False),
+        patches[0],
+        patches[1],
+    ):
+        probe.run_comm()
+    assert probe.body_ran
+    dbo_mocks["yield_switch"].assert_called_once_with()
+    dbo_mocks["switch_back"].assert_called_once_with()
+
+
+def test_comm_region_skipped_during_graph_capture(dbo_mocks):
+    probe = _RegionProbe()
+    patches = _patch_dbo_calls(dbo_mocks)
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=True),
+        patch.object(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=True),
+        patches[0],
+        patches[1],
+    ):
+        probe.run_comm()
+    assert probe.body_ran
+    dbo_mocks["yield_switch"].assert_not_called()
+    dbo_mocks["switch_back"].assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_comm_region_restores_compute_stream_on_error(dbo_mocks):
+    class _FailingProbe(_RegionProbe):
+        def run_comm(self) -> None:
+            with self._comm_region():
+                raise RuntimeError("collective failed")
+
+    probe = _FailingProbe()
+    patches = _patch_dbo_calls(dbo_mocks)
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=True),
+        patch.object(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=False),
+        patches[0],
+        patches[1],
+        pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="collective failed"),
+    ):
+        probe.run_comm()
+    dbo_mocks["yield_switch"].assert_called_once_with()
+    dbo_mocks["switch_back"].assert_called_once_with()
+
+
+def test_comm_overlap_active_requires_dbo_and_eager():
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=False),
+        patch.object(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=False),
+    ):
+        assert not _comm_overlap_active()
+    with (
+        patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=True),
+        patch.object(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=True),
+    ):
+        assert not _comm_overlap_active()
+
+
+def test_modular_subclass_supports_dbo_without_async():
+    inst = MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO()
+    # supports_async() also drives MK-internal shared-expert overlap, so it
+    # must not change with the DBO state.
+    for dbo_active in (False, True):
+        with patch.object(naive_dp_ep_rocm, "dbo_enabled", return_value=dbo_active):
+            assert not inst.supports_async()
+            assert inst.supports_dbo()
+
+
+def test_base_supports_dbo_follows_supports_async():
+    base = naive_dp_ep.MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular()
+    assert not base.supports_async()
+    assert not base.supports_dbo()
+    with patch.object(type(base), "supports_async", return_value=True):
+        assert base.supports_dbo()
+
+
+def test_factory_returns_rocm_subclass_on_rocm():
+    rocm_stub = SimpleNamespace(is_rocm=lambda: True)
+    with patch.object(naive_dp_ep, "current_platform", rocm_stub):
+        mono = make_moe_prepare_and_finalize_naive_dp_ep(use_monolithic=True)
+        modular = make_moe_prepare_and_finalize_naive_dp_ep(use_monolithic=False)
+    # No ROCm config selects a monolithic expert kernel on this path, so the
+    # monolithic variant falls back to the base class.
+    assert isinstance(mono, naive_dp_ep.MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPMonolithic)
+    assert isinstance(modular, MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO)
+
+
+def test_factory_returns_base_classes_elsewhere():
+    cuda_stub = SimpleNamespace(is_rocm=lambda: False)
+    with patch.object(naive_dp_ep, "current_platform", cuda_stub):
+        mono = make_moe_prepare_and_finalize_naive_dp_ep(use_monolithic=True)
+        modular = make_moe_prepare_and_finalize_naive_dp_ep(use_monolithic=False)
+    assert isinstance(mono, naive_dp_ep.MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPMonolithic)
+    assert isinstance(modular, naive_dp_ep.MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular)
+    assert not isinstance(modular, MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import threading
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.v1.worker import ubatching
+from vllm.v1.worker.ubatch_utils import maybe_create_ubatch_slices
+from vllm.v1.worker.ubatching import (
+    dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset,
+    make_ubatch_contexts,
+)
+
+
+def test_token_offset_without_dbo_context():
+    assert dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset() == 0
+
+
+def test_token_offset_defaults_to_zero():
+    ready_barrier = threading.Barrier(3)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Dual-batch-overlap (DBO) aware prepare/finalize for the naive DP/EP path.
+
+The naive path runs its DP all-gather (dispatch) and reduce-scatter (combine)
+synchronously on the calling stream. Under DBO that leaves the compute stream
+idle for the whole collective while the peer ubatch could be computing. This
+subclass hands each collective to the shared comm stream, using the same
+compute/comm handoff the DeepEP-HT prepare/finalize uses.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.naive_dp_ep import (
+    MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.ubatching import (
+    dbo_enabled,
+    dbo_switch_to_compute_sync,
+    dbo_yield_and_switch_from_compute_to_comm,
+)
+
+
+def _comm_overlap_active() -> bool:
+    # Graph capture must keep every collective on the capture stream: moving
+    # one to the comm stream changes the topology of the captured decode
+    # graph. Overlap is therefore limited to eager steps (prefill).
+    return dbo_enabled() and not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+
+
+class MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModularROCmDBO(
+    MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular
+):
+    """Modular naive DP/EP prepare/finalize with ROCm DBO comm overlap."""
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def _comm_region(self) -> Iterator[None]:
+        if not _comm_overlap_active():
+            yield
+            return
+        # Release the CPU to the peer ubatch so it can enqueue compute while
+        # this ubatch's collective runs; the compute stream waits on exit.
+        dbo_yield_and_switch_from_compute_to_comm()
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            dbo_switch_to_compute_sync()
+
+    def supports_dbo(self) -> bool:
+        # prepare()/finalize() hand the collective to the comm stream
+        # themselves, so the synchronous path is DBO-safe. supports_async()
+        # stays False: it also selects MK-internal shared-expert overlap.
+        return True

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for this. I reproduced the numbers and tested each part of the change on MI355X (8x, ROCm 10
nightly and the ROCm 7.2.3 nightly, DSV4-Pro, DP8, your launch flags, InferenceX agentic replay at
conc 64).

**Summary**

- The ~30% regression comes from a bug in main's DBO path rather than from the overlap: the eager
  microbatch threads never set their device, so work that uses the current device runs on GPU 0.
  One-line fix below; I'd like to see it go in with this PR.
- With the fix, DBO is at parity with no-DBO end to end (958 vs 917-977 output tok/s over three
  no-DBO runs), and accuracy matches with microbatching actually active (see section 2).
- I could reproduce the failures behind the `positions` slicing and the numpy-int casts. I could not
  reproduce the reasons given for disabling FULL-graph microbatching on ROCm or for the extra profile
  run.
- #46990's changes are gated on `deepep_high_throughput`, so they don't apply on this path.

### 1. Device not set in `_run_ubatches` threads

`_run_ubatches` starts a new thread per microbatch and never sets the device, so the thread's
current device is 0. `_capture_ubatches` already sets it:

```python
        def _ubatch_thread(results, model, ubatch_metadata):
            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(self.device)
            with ubatch_metadata.context:
```

Before the fix:
- With the server idle after startup, GPU 0 was 100% busy and the other seven idle (main: all idle).
- In kernel traces only rank 0's kernels were slow (fused MoE ~1.8x normal). DP ranks wait on each
  other every step, so every rank slows down, which matches the TPOT regression in the description.
- Agentic throughput: 670-717 tok/s with DBO before the fix, 958 after.
- On the ROCm 7.2.3 nightly, DBO without the fix crashed a worker with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`
  (0x1016) in 2 of 6 runs. With the fix, 4 of 4 runs were clean (931-955 tok/s vs 899-938 without
  DBO). Too few runs to call it fixed, and I haven't found the faulting kernel.

### 2. Comm-stream overlap for the naive DP/EP path

Performance: on a prefill-heavy burst (every rank on full 8192-token chunks), the comm stream's RCCL
kernels run on a separate HW queue and the collectives are almost entirely hidden; with them forced
back onto the compute stream the same burst is 20-75% slower (two runs). It is still ~9% slower than
not microbatching at all (3.67 s vs 3.37 s GPU time on rank 0, one clean run). The MoE and several
GEMM kernels run noticeably slower while RCCL overlaps them, so I suspect contention, but I haven't
isolated it.

How often it applies: microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks, so a step is only split if every
rank qualifies. In a gsm8k run with DBO on, most steps that met the threshold weren't split because
some rank opted out; as far as I can tell that was mostly FULL-graph decode (the check in section 3)
and, with prefix caching on, the prefix-cache hazard check. In the agentic replay ~8% of steps were
split at a threshold of 8192, so the end-to-end effect is small either way.

Accuracy: gsm8k (your test plan) and ARC-challenge matched main, but with prefix caching on, DBO
barely split any steps. With prefix caching off, ARC-challenge (25-shot) split ~70 steps and matched
main within error (acc 0.707 vs 0.715, acc_norm 0.730 vs 0.727, ±0.013). That covers prefill
log-likelihoods, not generation.

On the implementation, I'd suggest keeping this in the base class rather than adding a ROCm
subclass: the `_comm_region` handoff is a no-op without DBO, so it could live in
`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular` for all platforms, without the factory swap (which currently
changes the class for every ROCm naive DP/EP user) or the ROCm-only config check. And rather than
having `supports_async()` return `dbo_enabled()` to get past the modular-kernel assert, an explicit
"supports DBO" capability would say what's meant; `supports_async()` is also read by the
shared-experts scheduling on every forward, so overloading it has side effects beyond the assert.

Have you measured DBO with DP+EP on this model? That path already has an overlapping
dispatch/combine, and it would help to know how it compares before adding a second overlap path.
(If you do, note that #46990's ROCm-specific changes on that path, the async-scheduling disable, the
`comm_sms = 0` override and the post-dispatch/combine `synchronize()`, may be unnecessary and likely
cost performance; see the reasoning in ROCm/vllm@1e708140206bce5f0e518b636c7193c18f920bba and
ROCm/vllm@997dce5602326b08431ec28056452e9eb6f7b756. It may be worth trying with them reverted.)

### 3. Disabling microbatching for FULL cudagraphs on ROCm

With this hunk removed, microbatched FULL graphs captured and replayed without errors on both ROCm 10
and ROCm 7.2.3. Microbatched decode was ~1.8x slower per token, so keeping decode out of DBO is
right, but `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` already does that on any platform (with the hunk removed
and a high threshold, decode matched main). I'd drop the platform check. If you have the hipBLASLt
error text and ROCm version, I'd like to look at it.

### 4. Extra profile run on ROCm

With this removed I saw no "Workspace is locked" error, in long-prompt bursts or in a 900 s agentic
run. Do you have a failing config?

### 5. numpy int casts

Reproduced: without them startup fails with `TypeError: failed to specialize argument of type:
numpy.int32` in `build_c128a_topk_metadata`. The numpy value comes from the last split point in
`maybe_create_ubatch_slices`; casting there instead covers every consumer (tested in place of the
casts in this PR):

```python
    all_points = token_split_points + [int(cu_num_tokens[-1])]
```

### 6. Slicing `positions` per microbatch

Reproduced (startup fails with `positions is required for C128A metadata build`). Looks right.

### 7. MTP hidden-buffer offset

From reading the code this looks like a real bug: both microbatch threads write
`_mtp_hidden_buffer` from row 0, and the drafter reads the buffer in token order for the whole step.
It only affects draft quality, not output. The same write is in the other DeepSeek-V4 backends (and
DeepSeek-V4.1 / Qwen4-Exp); should they get the same offset?
@mawong-amd Thanks for your information, I will take a look.
